snippet.title: 🦃 Thanksgiving Prep! Make-Ahead Creamy Mashed Potatoes | Everything But the Turkey — Part 1 of 5 🥔
snippet.description:
🦃 EVERYTHING BUT THE TURKEY! PART 1 OF 5
🥔 Thanksgiving Prep Series — Mashed Potatoes

Thanksgiving is coming, and we’re getting a head start in the kitchen!

Welcome to Part 1 of my five-part series, Everything But the Turkey! We’re preparing some of our favorite Thanksgiving dishes, and I’m sharing a few tricks to help make the big day a little less hectic.

Because let’s be honest… there’s already enough going on in the kitchen on Thanksgiving Day! 😂

The secret? A little preparation the day before can save you so much time.

We’re kicking things off with one of the most important Thanksgiving sides: MASHED POTATOES! 🥔

🥔 INGREDIENTS

* 5 lbs Idaho or Yukon Gold potatoes
* ½ cup butter (1 stick)
* 1 cup sour cream
* Up to ½ cup heavy cream, optional
* 2 tsp salt, or to taste
* Black pepper, to taste

👩🏻‍🍳 PREPARATION — THE DAY BEFORE

1. Peel your potatoes and cut them into evenly sized chunks.
2. Place them in a large pot or bowl and cover completely with cold water.
3. Cover and refrigerate overnight.

Why do I do this? Soaking helps remove excess surface starch, which can help give you lighter, fluffier mashed potatoes.

👩🏻‍🍳 THE NEXT DAY

1. Drain the potatoes and rinse thoroughly with fresh water.
2. Transfer them to a large pot and cover with fresh water.
3. Add salt and bring to a boil.
4. Cook until fork-tender.
5. Drain the potatoes very well. This step is especially important if you’re using Yukon Gold potatoes because they can hold more moisture.
6. Add the butter and sour cream, then begin mashing.
7. If desired, slowly add up to ½ cup of warm heavy cream until you reach your preferred consistency.
8. Taste and adjust your salt and pepper.

You can use one cup of sour cream, or you can use sour cream with a little heavy cream. I personally love the combination, but you don’t need to use a large amount of both. The choice is yours!

❤️ SUMMER’S TIP: To prevent gooey mashed potatoes, make sure you properly strain them before mashing, especially when using Yukon Gold potatoes. Any excess water can make your potatoes too wet.

Also, don’t over-whip or overwork your potatoes! Mash just until they’re fluffy and creamy. If your potatoes do turn out too wet, you can add a small amount of instant mashed potato flakes to help absorb the excess moisture. That’s a pro tip!

And that’s Part 1! One Thanksgiving side down, four more to go.

👀 COMING UP IN PART 2: SWEET POTATOES! We’re getting those ready ahead of time, too, and I’ll show you how I finish them with all those delicious toppings!

#EverythingButTheTurkey #ThanksgivingPrep #SummersHomemadeMeals

snippet.title: I step on this mat and my feet finally exhale 👣
snippet.description:
There was a time when my feet felt like they carried the whole day for me. Heavy in the morning, achy by evening, and nothing I tried seemed to make a real difference.

So I started keeping the mat near my couch. Most nights I step on it barefoot for a few minutes, just breathing while the fabric and beads press into my soles. Sometimes I sit with it under my feet while the TV is on. Nothing complicated — just a few quiet minutes while the little nodes do their thing.

The first sessions felt intense, so I wore socks at first and kept them short. That helped me ease in without overdoing it.

Now it's the small pause I look forward to. My feet feel lighter afterward, like they got a proper reset, and the rest of me seems to follow.

If your feet have been asking for a little attention, this might be the few minutes they've been waiting for.

snippet.description:

Путин требует передела Европы, тем самым окончательно загоняя себя в ловушку. Оказавшись в плену своих фантазий относительно фронта, и поверив в бесконечную благосклонность Трампа, он хочет все больше и больше, считая себя чуть ли не гегемоном и вторым Сталиным. Пока экономика страны неуклонно летит в тартарары, а войска на фронте вообще не понимают, что им дальше делать. Любой следующий шаг ведет к еще большим потерям, проблемам и тупику. 

С вами Ян Матвеев и сегодня я расскажу, как Путин загнал себя в угол, расширяя требования на мирных переговорах по Украине. Находясь в крайне тяжелом положении, он пытается играть ва-банк, чтобы провернуть самый безумный блеф за все годы своего правления. Вот только его обман и никчемность требований очевидна практически всем. Как и шаткое положение — что на фронте, что в тылу. Об этом сегодня и поговорим.

snippet.title: The 10-Hour Movie That Trolled Britain!
snippet.description:
Paint Drying is a 2016 film by British filmmaker Charlie Shackleton (formerly known as Charlie Lyne). 

The 607-minute film consists of one continuous shot of white paint drying on a brick wall. It was created as a protest against the costs and practices of film classification in the United Kingdom.

The project was organized through a November 2015 Kickstarter campaign titled "Make the Censors Watch Paint Dry". 

At the time, the British Board of Film Classification (BBFC) charged filmmakers a submission fee of £101.50, plus £7.09 for every minute of footage. 

These costs could create a significant financial burden for independent filmmakers. Shackleton had previously paid £867.60 to get his documentary Beyond Clueless classified.

The final film ran for 607 minutes, or 10 hours and 7 minutes. BBFC examiners watched the film over two days, on 25 and 26 January 2016. 

It was subsequently awarded a U (Universal) classification, meaning it was suitable for audiences aged four and over.

The British Board of Film Classification was established in 1912 and is responsible for classifying films and other video content in the UK. 

Paint Drying is often discussed in the context of film censorship, independent cinema, experimental filmmaking, conceptual art and the economics of film distribution.

From a marketing perspective, Paint Drying is an unusual example of guerrilla marketing and unconventional promotion. 

By turning a protest against film classification fees into an absurd 10-hour film, Charlie Shackleton created a concept that attracted public attention and sparked conversations about independent filmmaking and creative expression. 

The project shows how an unexpected idea can generate publicity and turn a relatively niche issue into a widely discussed story.
